details:
Q1: How should a non-security issue declare that it depends on a PR?
Choices:
A) Make the hold generic. A trusted body (written by the pipeline account or by an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR) carries exactly one `- Depends on PR: #N` line and one `- Requires on main: <path> contains <fixed string>` line. Here that is #6667 and `scripts/ai_engine.sh` containing `_AI_ENGINE_EXIT_REFUSED`. The hold is released only when PR #N is merged into the default branch and the string is present on that branch. Anything malformed, repeated, untrusted or unreadable stays held. This reuses the clarify, implement and stall-poller hook points the security hold already uses. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Hard-code the condition (PR #6667 merged into main, plus `_AI_ENGINE_EXIT_REFUSED` in `scripts/ai_engine.sh` on main) in the gate. Issues opt in with a fixed marker.
C) Widen the existing `- Depends on: #N` line in `security_dependency.py` so non-security issues can use it and it accepts a PR number. The file-content check would be a separate fixed rule.
Q2: Which issues does the hold apply to, and where do the four feature tracks (capacity tiers, MEMORY_LEARNINGS, SOFT_ERROR_ANALYZER, JUDGE_INTERIM) come from?
Choices:
A) This issue delivers only the dependency hold and closes when its PR merges. The four feature tracks are filed as four separate standalone issues, by the pipeline account or a trusted maintainer, each carrying the declaration from Q1. The hold keeps them out of planning and implementation and out of the unblock scan. The poller resumes each one exactly once with a deduplicating marker. (RECOMMENDED)
B) This issue's PR uses `Refs #<this issue>` so the issue stays open. The hold applies to this issue, and once the conditions pass the poller resumes it a single time; re-planning then splits the work into the four issues.
C) Reopen #7186 after the hold merges and hold that issue instead; the four issues are created only after it resumes.
**Note:** B leaves one issue covering both the hold and the features, which conflicts with "permit only the dependency-gate repair" before the conditions pass. Pick B only if the re-plan is limited to splitting the work.
Q3: When a held issue meets its conditions, how should the poller resume it?
Choices:
A) Post one `/reclarify` with a per-issue release marker (e.g. `<!-- ai:pr-dependency-released:<n> -->`), mirroring the security hold. Only a marker from the pipeline account counts for deduplication. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Post one `/answer [auto-answered-by-poller]` so the issue goes straight to planning, using the existing Q1/Q2 answers.
C) Only remove the hold label and leave the issue for the normal stall poller to pick up.
